text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chinese Premier Li Peng urges Japan to safeguard Sino-Japanese relations.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat want President Bill Clinton to postpone a Middle East summit set to begin on Tuesday in Washington.
- Former Cabinet Minister S. Dhanabalan appointed chairman of Government investment arm Temasek Holdings, succeeding Lee Ek Tieng who stepped down.
- Survey by Straits Times shows combined net earnings of Singapore-listed companies rose 15 percent to Singapore $2.8 billion in first six months of this year.
- U.S. dollar hit 2 1/2 year high of 111.50 yen, boosted by signs Japan's economic recovery is faltering.

- Reports executive chairman of Ekran Bhd Ting Pek Khiing was hospitalised for a mild stroke last month raised fears about the Malaysian $13.6 billion Bakun dam and drove down share prices of five Malaysian listed companies.
- Engineering and infrastructure company Van Der Horst says it has set up joint venture company with two Indonesian partners to build S$204 million 24.5 km toll road in West Java.
- Group finance director Chris Cowan predicts trading profits for Jardine Matheson Holdings for 1996 will not match 1995.
- Hongkong based CM Telecom International Ltd is first company to make initial public offering on Singapore's newly set-up Foreign Board.
